rationale: The pain is acute and real — operators have lost actual money, giving strong willingness-to-pay signal from financial loss. The buyer is identifiable: a solo developer or small team lead already paying for AI API access, with a clear budget motive to prevent runaway costs. However, building a true cost-cap/circuit-breaker SDK or middleware layer requires real integration work (hooking into cloud billing APIs, agent runtimes, or at minimum an API proxy layer), putting buildability at 5 and operational autonomy at 5 — both short of the build gates. Validate first with a lightweight offering (a monitoring dashboard or alerting webhook) before committing to build.
solution_plan: The micro-service would be an AI Agent Cost Guardian: a lightweight monitoring and alerting layer that watches API spend in real time and sends alerts (email/Slack webhook) when a configurable budget threshold is crossed. BUILD: Claude can draft the monitoring logic and webhook integration; a simple landing page with a Stripe subscription link ($19-39/mo) and an intake form collecting the user's API keys and budget limits; Claude handles alert email drafting. SELL: reach indie hackers and solo devs via Hacker News Show HN, Twitter/X AI dev communities, and ProductHunt — Youval approves the outreach batch before it goes out. MAINTAIN: monitoring runs as a scheduled Claude task against billing APIs; alerts fire automatically; billing is Stripe recurring; support is Claude-drafted FAQ responses. ONLY recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing any unusual support escalations. Caveat: API key handling requires secure storage (a managed secret store), which adds integration complexity — validate that this is solvable before building.
notes: operational_autonomy (5) and buildability_with_ai (5) both fall below build gate floors (7 and 6 respectively). Stage capped at validate. Strong pain signal warrants validation outreach.
